speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked the Minister for National Development in respect of NParks’ revised typology that segregates selected stretches of the Park Connector Network into pedestrian-only paths and shared paths, whether NParks can study how to encourage safe and considerate use of such paths for different users, including those who are (i) on foot, (ii) using strollers, (iii) walking dogs, (iv) using wheelchairs and (v) using different types of active mobility devices, and for users to keep left or give way, to minimise accidents and improve user experience.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked the Minister for National Development in respect of NParks’ revised typology that segregates selected stretches of the Park Connector Network (PCN) into pedestrian-only paths and shared paths, whether NParks can consider the segregation of paths in a consistent manner and minimise frequent changes in the segregation of paths along similar stretches of PCN, including where the width of such paths have remained the same, so as to provide certainty and reduce confusion among users.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: These include signs to remind users to keep left when using the park connectors as well as markings that clearly indicate the different types of users allowed on each lane within the path, including pedestrians, cyclists and users of personal mobility devices.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: NParks works closely with the Land Transport Authority (LTA), the Friends of the PCN and the community to promote safe and gracious use of our PCN, especially for park connectors with high usage and more frequent feedback on user conflicts.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: NParks has also collaborated with the Singapore Kindness Movement to raise public awareness on PCN etiquette through its Kindness Ambassadors.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Just a bit of background for me asking this question, because I have spoken on this since 2018 and I have raised specifically in 2019 to 2021 regarding the new typology where, for the benefit of people listening to this, the new red lane markings for where one-third is exclusively for people on foot and about two-thirds for all users, including pedestrians, cyclists, mobility scooters, strollers, e-scooters and pets on leash.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I previously said that there are people walking on both lanes and not keeping left, and cyclists have to wait through the traffic, even going onto the exclusive walking lane, so to speak, because of congestion.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: I have previously asked for an increase in public education and enforcement efforts for safe and considerate use of the PCN.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Almost four years on, with actually some of the red lanes having faded and turned to yellow again, awaiting a new coat of paint, the situation has, in my view and my resident's view, remained the same, especially during the peak hours of usage.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: So, in the interest of safety and greater amenity of all PCN users – and I am grateful to the Minister of State for telling us about an update, that he is reviewing this – may I appeal to NParks or the Ministry of National Development (MND) to really review how we can improve on the use of the division of the lane, so that there is greater safety and greater amenity for all users?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: And moving forward, may I also ask NParks to increase its public education efforts on the use of this PCN for all users?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: On Question No 5, currently, some parts of the PCN have no red lane markings, while others have such red lane markings, and often it is all within a few hundred metres along same stretches.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Personally, I have observed that in some of these stretches, the width may not have varied.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: So, I would like to appeal to NParks to consider minimising different lane markings, different segregation of paths along similar stretches of PCN, to avoid confusion, perhaps adopting what LTA is doing with path segregation along its cycling network.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: And may I ask, where does NParks or MND provide advisories to PCN users on the revised typology and their intended users, and can these be made more prominent on the ground?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Hougang)
text: Because on the ground, I sense that people do not really understand how the division is meant to be used, even after all these years.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I can understand the issues raised by the Member.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I have been very fortunate to be involved in this area of work since I was in the Ministry of Transport and I can see how things have improved significantly over the years.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Members will realise that for behaviour to change, while we provide the infrastructure and we improve the markings, I think, as humans, we also will navigate this over time.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I can see that the behaviour has changed over time significantly.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We could see how the incidents and the behaviour of the people, with regard to how they use the PCN and even the cycling paths, have significantly changed and, that to me, is a positive move.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, I assure the Member that we will continue to do this.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And I am not sure whether I heard the Member correctly.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: He shared about some of the pedestrian paths being used by those on personal mobility devices and cyclists.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, essentially, during our pilot Phase 1, we have segregated them and what we have seen is that people are adjusting to this whole process.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And for some, it may seem that the width may be the same, but there are intersections where you would be required to understand the behaviour of people when they come together.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, it may not be as straightforward as the width.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: We look at various factors when we design it.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, I hope that the Member will join us in this journey to make sure that, while we are small, we maximise our land use.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: And what is key is this, a feedback that I heard from one of my counterparts recently is: "You are small, but you are able to use your land efficiently and the people are able to enjoy it even though they are all different types of users." So, we will continue to do this to make sure it brings goodness to Singaporeans.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: If I may just quickly build on the Parliamentary Question by my hon friend, Mr Dennis Tan, where he expressed some sense in which users are sometimes confused over the demarcations.

speaker: Assoc Prof Jamus Jerome Lim (Sengkang)
text: In that way, they will know for sure that they should be keeping left along the designated path for their use.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: I find that, even over time, I have seen people getting used to the markings.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, like what I shared with the Member earlier, it takes time for people to look at the changes and then adjust their behaviour.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: In the past, I remember when NParks first built it and started it, you realise that there were lots of people who did not know how to use it.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: But today, I walk or even cycle there at least three times a week, I realised that people are able to navigate better, there is less conflict along the path and, at the same time, when it comes to where users come in via the different paths into the PCN, you realise that they are able to look out for one another.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: So, we will take the feedback raised by the Members, but I want to urge Members to join us in this journey to make sure that we really develop something good for our people, so that wherever they live, they are able to enjoy the PCNs and even the shared and cycling paths that we have.
